summary_rationale: Yash Highvoltage remains India's only independent pure-play condenser-graded transformer bushing specialist, protected by 8-to-10-year utility qualification barriers, >96% repeat order rates, and a structural shift toward dry-type RIP bushings (86% of H1 FY27 revenue). Revenue compounded ~38% CAGR over FY22-FY26 to Rs 235.1 Cr and accelerated 95% YoY in H1 FY27 to Rs 194.5 Cr with 28.1% EBITDA margins, Rs 760+ Cr order book visibility, Rs 95 Cr net cash, and zero deviation certified by Acuite Ratings (14 Nov 2026) on the Rs 151 Cr preferential issue. Newly surfaced forensic watchpoints temper uncritical extrapolation: Q3/H2 FY27 indigenous RIP core commissioning at Jarod must execute before Swiss partner MGC Moser Glaser's mid-2027 supply sunset (no non-compete bar) to close a Rs 113.4 Cr FY26 net FX deficit; top-5 customers account for ~40-45% of revenue; promoter-family open-market disposals totaled 400,000 shares (~Rs 40.9 Cr) across Sep-Nov 2026 (including Keyur Shah's Nov 11-13 sales disclosed Nov 17); FY26 included a Rs 2.10 Cr vendor-email cyber-fraud control lapse; Hitachi Energy's Halol dry-bushing factory, US onshore capacity additions (HSP Charlotte, Hitachi Alamo), and USTR's 25 Nov 2026 proposed up-to-25% Section 301 tariffs on India tighten 2027-2028 export economics; and BSE SME listing constraints preclude Mainboard migration before December 2027.
